1 ## Sealed comparison (U57, U58) 2 - Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 to s19. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code, run by the pipeline from sealed argument vectors. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs, or from a published evaluator that runs on each arm's output without access to the arm's identity. Criteria, margins, thresholds, reference values and timeouts are fixed by a science step before the run, sealed, and unreadable by the run's agents and by the processes of arms and evaluator. Compute is recorded twice and never mixed: per invocation as attribution and per box allocation as the bill. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run; a design whose launch depends on an earlier run's outcomes is launched only when the science step finds them in that run's `C/comparison_scored.json`. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged. 3 - Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup, order_seed, timeout_s, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, bootstrap_resamples, comparisons}`: 4 - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what, commands, env}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual. 5 - `commands`: 1 to 8 commands, each a non-empty array of non-empty strings: the exact published command lines of the arm, in order, as argument vectors run without a shell. The pipeline runs them (see Evaluate); the arm's adapter only prepares. 6 - `env`: null or an object mapping names that match `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` and do not start with `CMP_` to strings; set for the arm's commands. 7 - Placeholders, in command and `env` strings only: `{input}` (the input id), `{run}`, `{out}` (the absolute paths of the invocation's `run/` and `out/`) and `{spec:

}` with `

` a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the input's `spec`, which must resolve in every input's `spec` to a string (inserted as is) or a finite number (inserted as `json.dumps` writes it). `{{` and `}}` stand for literal braces; any other `{` or `}` makes the design invalid. Substitution replaces every occurrence and is not repeated on its result. 8 - `inputs`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{id, spec}`: `id` a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; `spec` any JSON value (pins, case, configuration). 9 - `outputs`: 0 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, what, format, select}`: a logical result each arm, or the evaluator, writes for an input, compared across arms. `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `what` a non-empty string; `format` `"bytes"`, `"text_numbers"` (every number in the file's UTF-8 text, in order, as matched by `[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?` together with `nan`, `inf` and `-inf` tokens) or `"json_numbers"` (every number leaf of the JSON document, in document order; booleans are not numbers). `select` is null (the whole content) or, for `bytes` and `text_numbers` only, a Python `re` pattern with at least one capturing group: the content is read as UTF-8 with replacement, and the selected content is every group of every match of `re.finditer(select, text, re.MULTILINE)`, in order (an unmatched group as the empty string), joined by `"\n"`; `format` then applies to the selected content (`bytes` to its UTF-8 encoding). Several outputs may select different parts of the same file, each with its own comparison and tolerance. 10 - `metrics`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, unit, what, source, reduce, expect_count}`: `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `unit` and `what` non-empty strings; `source` `"trusted_wall"` or `"sealed_extraction"`. 11 - `trusted_wall`: the invocation's wall seconds: the adapter's wall plus its commands' walls, plus the evaluator's wall when the design has an evaluator. `reduce` and `expect_count` are null. 12 - `sealed_extraction`: read from fetched files by a rule the harness agent fixes before the run, reduced as the design states. `reduce` `"first"`, `"max"` or `"value_at_max_key"`; `expect_count` null or a positive integer, the number of matched values the rule must find. 13 - `evaluator`: null or exactly `{what, spec, timeout_s}`: a published, pinned program that reads one arm's output for one input, with data that only it may read, and writes evaluation files. `what` a non-empty string; `spec` any JSON value (program, pin, command, and where its private data come from); `timeout_s` null or a positive integer. 14 - `replicates` an integer from 1 to 30; `warmup` an integer from 0 to 3; `order_seed` and `bootstrap_seed` integers; `bootstrap_resamples` an integer from 1000 to 1000000; `budget_s` a positive integer, the evaluate stage's time budget for this comparison. When `args.run_ceiling_s` is present, `budget_s` must be below it. 15 - `timeout_s`: null, a positive integer for every invocation, or an object mapping every arm id to a positive integer or to an object mapping every input id to a positive integer: the cap of one invocation's arm part. 16 - `comparisons`: 0 to 12 items (0: a run that only records values and compute, for example to derive later reference values), each exactly `{id, arm, against, measure, criterion, direction, unit, pairing, rule, confidence, margin, threshold, strict, reference, missing, given, parts}`: 17 - `id` unique, matching `^K[0-9]{1,2}$`; `arm` an arm id; `against` a different arm id or `"reference"`; `parts` a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings. 18 - `measure` is exactly `{metric}` (a metric name) or exactly `{output, comparator}` (an output name and one of `"exact"`, `"elementwise_abs"`, `"elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max"`). An output comparison needs an arm as `against`. 19 - `criterion` `"agreement"` (every output comparison and no metric comparison), `"non_inferiority"`, `"superiority"` or `"ratio_at_least"`. 20 - `direction` `"higher_better"`, `"lower_better"` or `"two_sided"`: the metric as measured (for wall seconds, `lower_better`). `agreement` and `superiority` use `two_sided`; `non_inferiority` and `ratio_at_least` use `higher_better` or `lower_better`. 21 - `unit` `"pooled_mean"` (each replicate's value is the mean over inputs, decided once), `"per_input_all"` (decided per input; the comparison holds only if it holds on every input) or `"per_input_each"` (decided and reported per input). 22 - `pairing` `"paired_replicate"` or `"unpaired"`; `rule` `"all_pairs"` or `"bootstrap"`; `confidence` a number in `[0.5, 1)` for `bootstrap` and null for `all_pairs`. `ratio_at_least` uses exactly `pooled_mean`, `paired_replicate` and `bootstrap`; every other criterion uses `all_pairs` and a per-input unit; agreement uses `paired_replicate`. 23 - `margin`: for an output comparison, the comparator's tolerance: null for `exact`, `{"abs": x}` for `elementwise_abs`, `{"abs": x, "rel": y}` for `elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`. For `non_inferiority` and `superiority`, null or `{"abs": x}`. For `ratio_at_least`, null. `x` and `y` are finite and nonnegative. 24 - `threshold`: a finite number above 0 for `ratio_at_least`, otherwise null. `strict`: a boolean for `ratio_at_least` (true: the bound must exceed `threshold`; false: it may equal it), otherwise null. 25 - `reference`: exactly when `against` is `"reference"`, an object `{source, values}`: `source` a non-empty string naming where the values come from (for example an earlier run of this route and the rule that derived them), `values` mapping every input id to a finite number; otherwise null. A reference needs a metric `measure`, a per-input unit and `unpaired`. 26 - `missing`: `"void"` or `"fail"`, how a missing value is decided (see Scoring). 27 - `given`: an array, possibly empty, of unique ids of comparisons that come earlier in `comparisons`; a decision unit is decided only when each of them is supported for it (see Scoring). 28 An invalid argument or design, or a path that cannot be read as JSON, fails intake with `error_class: parse` before any agent call. 29 - Before the intake agent call and any box command, the pipeline writes atomically, in this order: `C/comparison.json`, exactly `{source, source_sha256, design}`; `C/comparison_seal.json`, exactly `{comparison_sha256, sealed_utc}` (the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of `C/comparison.json`); and `A/comparison_view.json`, exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup}` copied from the design, with `evaluator` reduced to `{what, spec}` (null when the design's is null). The view holds no comparison, criterion, margin, threshold, reference value, timeout, part, seed or budget. Agents see only the view; comparison-mode prompts name it and never `C/` or the design path. The science step that writes the design is responsible for the view's free text (`what`, `spec`, `select`) stating no expectation, criterion or result, and for keeping no copy of the design on the pipeline host outside the paths hidden below. 30 - Isolation of agent calls, comparison mode only. Every agent call of the run (intake, harness, and every setup and anchors repair) is dispatched with wf `isolation` (see Implement) as implement's calls are: `directory` a fresh private view created for that call under the system temporary directory, `box_access` false, and `hidden` holding the run root, the workflow journal directory, the design file's parent directory and, when the design file lies inside a git work tree, that work tree's top-level directory (the nearest ancestor that contains `.git`). Under `isolation` the rest of the host is read-only and the view is the only writable host directory, so each role gets copies of what it reads today and writes only into its view; the pipeline copies its results back: 31 - intake view: `comparison_view.json`; when the brief is a file, `brief/` (a copy of its bytes), which the prompt names in place of the brief's path; and an empty `intake/`. After the call the pipeline copies each regular file directly under the view's `intake/` (no symbolic link, no subdirectory) to `A/intake/`. 32 - harness view: `comparison_view.json`, `intake/` (a copy of `A/intake/`) and an empty `harness/`; the probe stays in the prompt as today. After the call the pipeline copies each regular file directly under the view's `harness/`, and each regular file `harness/arms/.sh`, to the same name under `A/harness/`. 33 - setup or anchors repair view: `comparison_view.json`, `intake/` and `harness/` (copies of `A/intake/` and `A/harness/`); the probe and log tail stay in the prompt. After the call the pipeline copies back only the scripts that repair may rewrite today (`setup.sh`; or `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh`), and discards every other change, as the existing restore of protected scripts does. 34 Prompts name the view's paths in place of `A/intake/` and `A/harness/`. Network access is unchanged by `isolation`. A call that cannot be dispatched so fails as an isolation failure does; there is no fallback. Views are removed after the stage. 35 - Intake prompt, comparison mode only: the run compares the view's arms on the view's inputs; `A0` is the benchmark intake records as usual; intake also records, in `benchmark.json` under the key `arms`, each other arm's published source, pin and commands, under the key `evaluator` the evaluator's published source, pin and command when the view has one, and in `data.json` every input any arm or the evaluator needs, marking the evaluator's private data. 36 - Harness prompt, comparison mode only: `setup.sh` also builds or installs every arm's published program and configuration, and the evaluator, as published, under the shared run directory or with apt, never under the home directory. `setup.sh` places every file only the evaluator may read under the top-level directory `cmp-private/` of the shared run directory and nowhere else. The harness agent writes, besides the usual scripts: 37 - one adapter `harness/arms/.sh` per arm, `A0` included, which only prepares the invocation (stages the input named by `CMP_INPUT` under `run/` or `CMP_OUT`) and never runs the arm's program, writes or patches source, or computes, writes or asserts a metric; 38 - when the view has an evaluator, `harness/evaluate.sh`, which runs the published, pinned evaluator on the arm output in `CMP_ARM_OUT` for the input named by `CMP_INPUT`, reads private data only under `CMP_PRIVATE`, writes its results under `CMP_EVAL_OUT`, and never writes elsewhere; 39 - `harness/cmp_files.json`, exactly `{"files": {...}}`, mapping each arm id to an object that maps every output name to a location: a relative path, or exactly `{glob}` with `glob` a pattern of relative-path components that may also use `*`, `?`, `[` and `]`. Locations are relative to the invocation directory, and their first component is `out` (the arm's files) or `eval` (the evaluator's files); 40 - `harness/cmp_extract.json`, exactly `{"rules": [...]}`, one rule per arm and `sealed_extraction` metric, each exactly `{arm, metric, file, kind, expr}`, with `file` a relative path whose first component is `out` or `eval`, and `kind` and `expr` as defined for `harness/card_extract.json` (U54), extended by the metric's `reduce`: `kind` `"json"`: `expr` points to a finite number, to an array of finite numbers, or (for `value_at_max_key`) to an array of two-element arrays `[key, value]` of finite numbers; `kind` `"regex"`: exactly one capturing group, or exactly two (key, then value) for `value_at_max_key`; 41 - `harness/versions.sh`, which prints one JSON object mapping each arm id, and `"evaluator"` when the view has one, to exactly `{version, executable}`: the program's version string and the path, absolute or relative to the shared run directory, of its main executable file. 42 Relative paths are one or more `/`-separated components made of `[A-Za-z0-9._+=-]`, none `.` or `..`. `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` keep their meaning for `A0`. 43 - After harness generation or copy (with `args.harness_from`, the source directory must also hold `arms/`, `cmp_files.json`, `cmp_extract.json`, `versions.sh` and, when the design has an evaluator, `evaluate.sh`, copied like the scripts) and before the harness upload, those files must exist and be valid: `harness/arms/` holds exactly one non-empty adapter per arm; `evaluate.sh` exists exactly when the design has an evaluator; `cmp_files.json` maps every arm and every output, with `eval` locations only when the design has an evaluator; and `cmp_extract.json` has exactly one rule per arm and `sealed_extraction` metric, whose group count matches the metric's `reduce`. Otherwise reproduce fails with `error_class: parse` before the upload. The pipeline then writes `C/arms_seal.json`, exactly `{files, sealed_utc}`, mapping each of those files' names (adapters as `arms/.sh`) to the SHA-256 of its bytes. They upload with the harness, in the same encoding. No repair changes them. 44 - When the design has an evaluator, a probe whose `sudo_nopasswd` is not true fails reproduce with `error_class: infra` right after the probe, before the harness call: the separated users below need it. The rule that harness scripts use sudo only for apt is unchanged; only the pipeline's trusted scripts below use it otherwise. 45 - In comparison mode reproduce runs exactly as usual for `A0`. Profile, seal, propose and implement are SKIPPED. Evaluate runs the comparison when reproduce passed, and is SKIPPED otherwise, as after any failed gate. 46 - Evaluate, comparison mode (U57): 47 - Separated users, only when the design has an evaluator: one box command, operation `comparison-users`, runs the trusted `bash profiler/cmp_users.sh` (written inline by the pipeline). With `sudo -n`, it creates, when absent, two system users without login shell or home, `cmp-arm` and `cmp-eval`; adds both to every group that owns a `/dev/nvidia*` device file; recursively removes group and other write access from the shared run directory and grants other users read access to every file and search access to every directory in it, except `cmp-private`; and makes `cmp-private` (created empty when absent) and everything under it owned by `cmp-eval`, with the directory at mode `700`. It then checks that `sudo -n -u nvidia-smi -L` prints, for each of the two users, the same number of GPU lines as for the box user, and that `sudo -n -u cmp-arm test -r cmp-private` fails. Any failure fails evaluate with `error_class: infra` before any invocation. The arm part therefore cannot read the evaluator's private data, cannot write any file the evaluator or the wrapper runs, and cannot change modes that protect them, whatever its adapter or commands do. 48 - Versions: one box command, operation `versions`, runs `bash harness/versions.sh` with stdout to `out/comparison/versions.json`, then the trusted `python3 profiler/cmp_system.py` (written inline by the pipeline) writes `out/comparison/system.json`, exactly `{cpu_model, cpu_logical, kernel, driver_version, cuda_version, gpus, executables}`: `lscpu` model name and logical CPU count; `uname -r`; the driver and CUDA versions that `nvidia-smi` reports; `gpus` one row per GPU, exactly `{index, name, uuid, memory_total}`, from `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,uuid,memory.total --format=csv,noheader`; and `executables` mapping each key of `versions.json` to exactly `{version, executable, sha256, libraries}`, with `sha256` the SHA-256 of the executable's resolved file and `libraries` one row per `ldd` line of the form ` => ...`, exactly `{name, path, sha256}` (the resolved file's SHA-256), or `[]` when `ldd` fails or reports a static executable. Any field that cannot be read is null. 49 - Rounds: `warmup` warmup rounds, then `replicates` replicate rounds. Each round runs every (arm, input) pair once, in an order drawn from one `random.Random(order_seed)` stream: one `shuffle` of the round's pairs per round, warmups included. Invocation `k` (from 1, in run order, warmups included) has the token `i`, which names it on the box; no box path, file name, process argument or environment variable that the evaluator part can read names the arm. 50 - Each invocation is two box commands from the shared run directory. First, operation `comparison-job` writes the job file `comparison-jobs/i.json`, exactly `{arm, input, mode, round, arm_timeout_s, eval_timeout_s}` (mode `warmup` or `replicate`; the timeouts resolved as under Timeouts when this command starts), in the harness upload encoding, with the file at mode `600` in a directory at mode `700`, both owned by the box user. Second, operation `comparison` runs the trusted wrapper `python3 profiler/cmp_wrap.py i` (written inline by the pipeline, as the profile stage writes its probe), whose only argument is the token. The wrapper reads its job file and builds a fresh invocation directory `comparison-work/i/` at mode `711`, holding `run/` (a symbolic link to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work`, `evaluation-work`, `units-check`, `comparison-work`, `comparison-jobs` and `cmp-private`), an empty `out/`, an empty `eval/`, and empty `home/` and `ehome/`. The part user is `cmp-arm` for the arm part and `cmp-eval` for the evaluator part when the design has an evaluator, and the box user otherwise. With separated users, `run/`, `out/` and `home/` are owned by `cmp-arm`, and `eval/` and `ehome/` by `cmp-eval`. A part runs as `sudo -n -u -- env -i ` with separated users, and directly otherwise; its variables are the wrapper's environment without any `CMP_`, `SUDO_` or `HOME` name, with `HOME` set to `home/` (arm part) or `ehome/` (evaluator part), plus the part's `CMP_` variables below. The wrapper: 51 1. arm part: runs `bash harness/arms/.sh` with working directory `run/`; then, when the adapter exits 0, runs each of the arm's commands in order with working directory `run/`, after placeholder substitution and with the arm's `env`, with standard output and error written to `out/cmd.stdout` and `out/cmd.stderr` (`k` from 1), stopping at the first nonzero exit. A first argument containing `/` resolves relative to `run/`, otherwise through `PATH`. Its variables are `CMP_INPUT` (the input id), `CMP_INPUT_SPEC` (the JSON of that input's `spec`) and `CMP_OUT` (the absolute path of `out/`); 52 2. with separated users, after the arm part: kills every process of `cmp-arm` (`pkill -KILL -u cmp-arm`) once per second until `pgrep -u cmp-arm` finds none, for at most the time left in `budget_s` (processes still left make the invocation `invalid`); makes `run/` and `out/` and everything under them owned by the box user; makes the invocation `invalid` when `out/` holds anything other than regular files and directories (a symbolic link included); then removes group and other write access and grants other users read and search access under `out/`; 53 3. evaluator part, only when the design has an evaluator and the arm part's status is `ok`: runs `bash /harness/evaluate.sh` with the shared run directory as working directory and the variables `CMP_INPUT`, `CMP_INPUT_SPEC`, `CMP_ARM_OUT` (the absolute path of `out/`), `CMP_EVAL_OUT` (the absolute path of `eval/`) and `CMP_PRIVATE` (the absolute path of `cmp-private`); then kills every process of `cmp-eval` as in step 2 and makes `eval/` and everything under it owned by the box user; 54 4. writes `wrap.json` in the invocation directory, atomically and last, at mode `600`, exactly `{status, adapter_rc, adapter_wall_s, commands, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_status, eval_rc, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, eval_gpu_busy_known}`. `status` is `"ok"` (the adapter and every command exited 0), `"failed"` (a nonzero exit), `"timeout"` or `"invalid"`; `commands` has one row per command started, exactly `{argv, rc, wall_s, executable, sha256}` (the substituted argument vector, exit status, `perf_counter` wall seconds, the resolved executable path and its SHA-256, null when unresolved); `eval_status` is `"ok"`, `"failed"`, `"timeout"` or `"skipped"` (no evaluator, or the arm part was not `ok`). Walls are `perf_counter` seconds and exit statuses null on timeout. GPU-busy seconds are sampled separately for the arm part and the evaluator part (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu` immediately and every second; each finite sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100` seconds, summed over GPUs; the matching `known` flag is false when no valid sample was taken). 55 The invocation's `out/`, `eval/` and `wrap.json` are fetched to `A/results/evaluate/comparison/ or r>///` (`r` the round index), from the pipeline's own record of each token's job. 56 - Timeouts: the arm part's timeout is the smallest of its `timeout_s` (when non-null), the time left in `budget_s`, and the time left before the run ceiling; the evaluator part's is the smallest of `evaluator.timeout_s` (when non-null) and the same two. On a timeout the wrapper kills the part's whole process group (with separated users, every process of the part user, as in step 2) and records `"timeout"`. When the time left in `budget_s` is below 1 s, the remaining invocations are not run, and their status is `"not_run"`. A missing or invalid `wrap.json` gives status `"invalid"`. 57 - Values: for an invocation with status `ok`, a `trusted_wall` metric is `adapter_wall_s` plus its commands' `wall_s`, plus `eval_wall_s` when the design has an evaluator (null unless `eval_status` is `ok`). A `sealed_extraction` metric is its rule applied to the fetched file: the matched values are every `float()`-parsed match of the regex in order, or the number or array at the pointer. With `reduce` `first` or `max`, the value is that function of the matched values; with `value_at_max_key`, it is the value of the first pair whose key is the largest. A file under `eval` needs `eval_status` `ok`. A missing or unreadable file, no match, a nonfinite matched number, or a match count other than a non-null `expect_count` gives null. Every value of an invocation with any other status is null. A null value is a missing value. 58 - Compute (G6): `A/results/evaluate/comparison_compute.json`, written atomically after the last invocation, is exactly `{invocations, arms, all_invocations, system, versions, allocation}`. 59 - `invocations` has one row per scheduled invocation in run order, each exactly `{round, arm, input, status, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_status, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, attributed_usd}`, from `wrap.json`: `wall_s` is `adapter_wall_s` plus the commands' walls, and `attributed_usd` is `(wall_s + eval_wall_s) / 3600 * C/box.json.price_usd_h`, with a null wall counted as 0 and null when the price is unavailable. Rows of `not_run` invocations have null numbers. 60 - `arms` has one row per arm, each exactly `{arm, invocations, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, attributed_usd}`, summed over that arm's replicate invocations whatever their status, with a null counted as 0; `gpu_busy_known` is true only when every summed row's flag is. 61 - `all_invocations` is exactly `{invocations, wall_s, eval_wall_s, attributed_usd}`, summed over every row, warmups and failures included, with a null counted as 0. 62 - `system` and `versions` copy the fetched `system.json` and `versions.json` (null when missing or invalid). 63 - `allocation` is the bill of the whole box allocation, which may include work outside this run, exactly `{type, price_usd_h, started_utc, ended_utc, hours, usd, final}` from `C/box.json`. When that record has `ended_utc` and `hours`, they are copied and `final` is true; otherwise `ended_utc` is null, `hours` is the time from `started_utc` to when the file is written, and `final` is false. `usd` is `hours * price_usd_h`. Unavailable fields are null. At takeaways, after a matching allocation record refreshes `C/box.json` (see Compute metadata), the pipeline rewrites the file atomically with only `allocation` recomputed. The run's own share stays `run_box_usd`. 64 Uploads, links, job files, user setup and fetches are outside every invocation row; they remain in the stage's receipts. 65 - Scoring (U58): after the last invocation, `python3 -I m5/score_comparison.py `. It checks the SHA-256 of `C/comparison.json` against `C/comparison_seal.json` and of each sealed harness file against `C/arms_seal.json`, then scores each comparison, in design order, from the replicate rounds only. 66 - Locations: a relative path names one file. A `{glob}` location names the regular files that Python `glob.glob(glob, root_dir=)` returns, sorted by a key that splits the relative path into runs of digits and non-digits, compares digit runs as integers and breaks ties by the path; their contents, each after `select`, are joined by `"\n"` (by `b"\n"` for `bytes`). A side of an (input, replicate) pair is missing when its invocation's status is not `ok`, when the location is under `eval` and `eval_status` is not `ok`, when the location names no file or an unreadable one, when the content cannot be parsed as the output's `format`, or when the selected content is empty (no bytes for `bytes`, no numbers otherwise). 67 - Output comparisons (`agreement`): for each input and replicate where neither side is missing, the comparator compares the two contents. `exact`: identical bytes. Otherwise both contents are parsed as the output's `format` into number lists; different lengths, or a NaN in one list but not at the same position in the other, disagree; equal infinities agree; finite pairs agree when `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol` (`elementwise_abs`) or `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol + rel_tol * max(abs(a), abs(b))` (`elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`). A pair agrees when every element agrees. Each compared pair records `max_abs_error` and `max_rel_error` over its finite elements (null when none). 68 - Metric comparisons: an arm's value for (replicate, input) is the metric value above. For `pooled_mean`, a replicate's value is the mean over inputs, null when any input's value is null. Per decision unit (the pooled value, or each input): for `paired_replicate`, the differences are `arm - against` per replicate; for `unpaired`, the differences of every arm value with every against value, or of every arm value with the input's reference value. `ratio_at_least` uses the ratio of means `mean(arm) / mean(against)` for `higher_better` and `mean(against) / mean(arm)` for `lower_better`. 69 - Missing values, per decision unit: `n_missing` counts the arm's missing values and, against an arm, the against arm's (for `pooled_mean` a replicate counts once; for agreement a pair with a missing side counts once). With `"void"`, any missing value makes the unit void with reason `"missing_values"`. With `"fail"`, a missing value of `arm` makes the unit `"not_supported"` with reason `"missing_values"`, and otherwise a missing value of `against` makes it void with reason `"missing_values"`. 70 - Eligibility (`given`): for each listed comparison, its outcome for this unit is that comparison's row for the same input when both comparisons are decided per input, and otherwise that comparison's outcome, where `"per_input"` counts as supported only when every row is. When any of these is not `"supported"`, the unit is void with reason `"not_eligible"`. 71 - Interval: for `all_pairs`, `[lo, hi]` is the minimum and maximum of the differences, and needs at least one difference. For `bootstrap`, the ratio of means is recomputed on `bootstrap_resamples` resamples (`B`) with replacement of the unit's paired replicates, drawn from one `random.Random(bootstrap_seed)` stream in comparison order, and `[lo, hi]` is the `(1 - confidence) / 2` and `(1 + confidence) / 2` empirical quantiles (sorted resamples, index `floor(q * (B - 1))`); it needs at least two replicates. `estimate` is the mean difference (`all_pairs`) or the ratio of means (`bootstrap`) on the full data. Too few values gives outcome `"void"` with reason `"insufficient_replicates"`. 72 - Margin value `m`: 0 for a null margin, `x` for `{"abs": x}`. 73 - Outcome per decision unit, in this order: eligibility; then, for agreement, any compared pair that disagrees makes the unit not supported; then the missing-value rule; then the interval's minimum count; then the criterion. The criterion gives `"supported"`, `"not_supported"` or else `"inconclusive"`: agreement is supported when at least one pair was compared, every compared pair agrees and none is missing (with no compared pair, it is void with reason `"missing_values"`); non-inferiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo >= -m`, not supported when `hi < -m`; non-inferiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi <= m`, not supported when `lo > m`; superiority (`two_sided`) is supported when `lo > m` or `hi < -m`, not supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`; ratio with `strict` false is supported when `lo >= threshold`, not supported when `hi < threshold`; ratio with `strict` true is supported when `lo > threshold`, not supported when `hi <= threshold`. 74 - `sign` of a unit is `"higher"` when a superiority is supported with `lo > m`, `"lower"` when it is supported with `hi < -m`, and null otherwise. 75 - A comparison's outcome: for `pooled_mean`, its one unit's outcome; for `per_input_all`, supported when every input is supported, not supported when any input is not supported, void when any input is void and none is not supported, otherwise inconclusive; for `per_input_each`, `"per_input"`, with each input's outcome in its rows. 76 - `C/comparison_scored.json`, atomic, is exactly `{comparison_sha256, comparisons, totals}`. `comparisons` follows the design's order, each exactly `{id, arm, against, criterion, unit, outcome, rows}`; `rows` has one row per decision unit (`input` null for `pooled_mean`), each exactly `{input, n, n_missing, estimate, lo, hi, margin_value, threshold, outcome, sign, reason, pairs}`. `n` counts the differences, ratios or compared pairs; `pairs` is null for metric comparisons and, for agreement, the per-replicate rows `{replicate, agrees, missing, max_abs_error, max_rel_error}` (`agrees` null and `missing` true when a side is missing). Numbers are null when void; `reason` is `"missing_values"`, `"insufficient_replicates"` or `"not_eligible"` for a void unit, `"missing_values"` for a unit made not supported by the `"fail"` rule, and null otherwise. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons. 77 - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. A missing or invalid `wrap.json` or fetched file is not invalid input; it is a missing value. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`. 78 - Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. Evaluate facts keep every existing key, null in comparison mode. 79

## Sealed comparison (U57, U58) - Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 to s19. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code, run by the pipeline from sealed argument vectors. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs, or from a published evaluator that runs on each arm's output without access to the arm's identity. Criteria, margins, thresholds, reference values and timeouts are fixed by a science step before the run, sealed, and unreadable by the run's agents and by the processes of arms and evaluator. Compute is recorded twice and never mixed: per invocation as attribution and per box allocation as the bill. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run; a design whose launch depends on an earlier run's outcomes is launched only when the science step finds them in that run's `C/comparison_scored.json`. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged. - Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup, order_seed, timeout_s, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, bootstrap_resamples, comparisons}`: - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what, commands, env}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual. - `commands`: 1 to 8 commands, each a non-empty array of non-empty strings: the exact published command lines of the arm, in order, as argument vectors run without a shell. The pipeline runs them (see Evaluate); the arm's adapter only prepares. - `env`: null or an object mapping names that match `^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$` and do not start with `CMP_` to strings; set for the arm's commands. - Placeholders, in command and `env` strings only: `{input}` (the input id), `{run}`, `{out}` (the absolute paths of the invocation's `run/` and `out/`) and `{spec:

}` with `

` a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into the input's `spec`, which must resolve in every input's `spec` to a string (inserted as is) or a finite number (inserted as `json.dumps` writes it). `{{` and `}}` stand for literal braces; any other `{` or `}` makes the design invalid. Substitution replaces every occurrence and is not repeated on its result. - `inputs`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{id, spec}`: `id` a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; `spec` any JSON value (pins, case, configuration). - `outputs`: 0 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, what, format, select}`: a logical result each arm, or the evaluator, writes for an input, compared across arms. `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `what` a non-empty string; `format` `"bytes"`, `"text_numbers"` (every number in the file's UTF-8 text, in order, as matched by `[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?` together with `nan`, `inf` and `-inf` tokens) or `"json_numbers"` (every number leaf of the JSON document, in document order; booleans are not numbers). `select` is null (the whole content) or, for `bytes` and `text_numbers` only, a Python `re` pattern with at least one capturing group: the content is read as UTF-8 with replacement, and the selected content is every group of every match of `re.finditer(select, text, re.MULTILINE)`, in order (an unmatched group as the empty string), joined by `"\n"`; `format` then applies to the selected content (`bytes` to its UTF-8 encoding). Several outputs may select different parts of the same file, each with its own comparison and tolerance. - `metrics`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, unit, what, source, reduce, expect_count}`: `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `unit` and `what` non-empty strings; `source` `"trusted_wall"` or `"sealed_extraction"`. - `trusted_wall`: the invocation's wall seconds: the adapter's wall plus its commands' walls, plus the evaluator's wall when the design has an evaluator. `reduce` and `expect_count` are null. - `sealed_extraction`: read from fetched files by a rule the harness agent fixes before the run, reduced as the design states. `reduce` `"first"`, `"max"` or `"value_at_max_key"`; `expect_count` null or a positive integer, the number of matched values the rule must find. - `evaluator`: null or exactly `{what, spec, timeout_s}`: a published, pinned program that reads one arm's output for one input, with data that only it may read, and writes evaluation files. `what` a non-empty string; `spec` any JSON value (program, pin, command, and where its private data come from); `timeout_s` null or a positive integer. - `replicates` an integer from 1 to 30; `warmup` an integer from 0 to 3; `order_seed` and `bootstrap_seed` integers; `bootstrap_resamples` an integer from 1000 to 1000000; `budget_s` a positive integer, the evaluate stage's time budget for this comparison. When `args.run_ceiling_s` is present, `budget_s` must be below it. - `timeout_s`: null, a positive integer for every invocation, or an object mapping every arm id to a positive integer or to an object mapping every input id to a positive integer: the cap of one invocation's arm part. - `comparisons`: 0 to 12 items (0: a run that only records values and compute, for example to derive later reference values), each exactly `{id, arm, against, measure, criterion, direction, unit, pairing, rule, confidence, margin, threshold, strict, reference, missing, given, parts}`: - `id` unique, matching `^K[0-9]{1,2}$`; `arm` an arm id; `against` a different arm id or `"reference"`; `parts` a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings. - `measure` is exactly `{metric}` (a metric name) or exactly `{output, comparator}` (an output name and one of `"exact"`, `"elementwise_abs"`, `"elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max"`). An output comparison needs an arm as `against`. - `criterion` `"agreement"` (every output comparison and no metric comparison), `"non_inferiority"`, `"superiority"` or `"ratio_at_least"`. - `direction` `"higher_better"`, `"lower_better"` or `"two_sided"`: the metric as measured (for wall seconds, `lower_better`). `agreement` and `superiority` use `two_sided`; `non_inferiority` and `ratio_at_least` use `higher_better` or `lower_better`. - `unit` `"pooled_mean"` (each replicate's value is the mean over inputs, decided once), `"per_input_all"` (decided per input; the comparison holds only if it holds on every input) or `"per_input_each"` (decided and reported per input). - `pairing` `"paired_replicate"` or `"unpaired"`; `rule` `"all_pairs"` or `"bootstrap"`; `confidence` a number in `[0.5, 1)` for `bootstrap` and null for `all_pairs`. `ratio_at_least` uses exactly `pooled_mean`, `paired_replicate` and `bootstrap`; every other criterion uses `all_pairs` and a per-input unit; agreement uses `paired_replicate`. - `margin`: for an output comparison, the comparator's tolerance: null for `exact`, `{"abs": x}` for `elementwise_abs`, `{"abs": x, "rel": y}` for `elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`. For `non_inferiority` and `superiority`, null or `{"abs": x}`. For `ratio_at_least`, null. `x` and `y` are finite and nonnegative. - `threshold`: a finite number above 0 for `ratio_at_least`, otherwise null. `strict`: a boolean for `ratio_at_least` (true: the bound must exceed `threshold`; false: it may equal it), otherwise null. - `reference`: exactly when `against` is `"reference"`, an object `{source, values}`: `source` a non-empty string naming where the values come from (for example an earlier run of this route and the rule that derived them), `values` mapping every input id to a finite number; otherwise null. A reference needs a metric `measure`, a per-input unit and `unpaired`. - `missing`: `"void"` or `"fail"`, how a missing value is decided (see Scoring). - `given`: an array, possibly empty, of unique ids of comparisons that come earlier in `comparisons`; a decision unit is decided only when each of them is supported for it (see Scoring). An invalid argument or design, or a path that cannot be read as JSON, fails intake with `error_class: parse` before any agent call. - Before the intake agent call and any box command, the pipeline writes atomically, in this order: `C/comparison.json`, exactly `{source, source_sha256, design}`; `C/comparison_seal.json`, exactly `{comparison_sha256, sealed_utc}` (the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of `C/comparison.json`); and `A/comparison_view.json`, exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, evaluator, replicates, warmup}` copied from the design, with `evaluator` reduced to `{what, spec}` (null when the design's is null). The view holds no comparison, criterion, margin, threshold, reference value, timeout, part, seed or budget. Agents see only the view; comparison-mode prompts name it and never `C/` or the design path. The science step that writes the design is responsible for the view's free text (`what`, `spec`, `select`) stating no expectation, criterion or result, and for keeping no copy of the design on the pipeline host outside the paths hidden below. - Isolation of agent calls, comparison mode only. Every agent call of the run (intake, harness, and every setup and anchors repair) is dispatched with wf `isolation` (see Implement) as implement's calls are: `directory` a fresh private view created for that call under the system temporary directory, `box_access` false, and `hidden` holding the run root, the workflow journal directory, the design file's parent directory and, when the design file lies inside a git work tree, that work tree's top-level directory (the nearest ancestor that contains `.git`). Under `isolation` the rest of the host is read-only and the view is the only writable host directory, so each role gets copies of what it reads today and writes only into its view; the pipeline copies its results back: - intake view: `comparison_view.json`; when the brief is a file, `brief/` (a copy of its bytes), which the prompt names in place of the brief's path; and an empty `intake/`. After the call the pipeline copies each regular file directly under the view's `intake/` (no symbolic link, no subdirectory) to `A/intake/`. - harness view: `comparison_view.json`, `intake/` (a copy of `A/intake/`) and an empty `harness/`; the probe stays in the prompt as today. After the call the pipeline copies each regular file directly under the view's `harness/`, and each regular file `harness/arms/.sh`, to the same name under `A/harness/`. - setup or anchors repair view: `comparison_view.json`, `intake/` and `harness/` (copies of `A/intake/` and `A/harness/`); the probe and log tail stay in the prompt. After the call the pipeline copies back only the scripts that repair may rewrite today (`setup.sh`; or `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh`), and discards every other change, as the existing restore of protected scripts does. Prompts name the view's paths in place of `A/intake/` and `A/harness/`. Network access is unchanged by `isolation`. A call that cannot be dispatched so fails as an isolation failure does; there is no fallback. Views are removed after the stage. - Intake prompt, comparison mode only: the run compares the view's arms on the view's inputs; `A0` is the benchmark intake records as usual; intake also records, in `benchmark.json` under the key `arms`, each other arm's published source, pin and commands, under the key `evaluator` the evaluator's published source, pin and command when the view has one, and in `data.json` every input any arm or the evaluator needs, marking the evaluator's private data. - Harness prompt, comparison mode only: `setup.sh` also builds or installs every arm's published program and configuration, and the evaluator, as published, under the shared run directory or with apt, never under the home directory. `setup.sh` places every file only the evaluator may read under the top-level directory `cmp-private/` of the shared run directory and nowhere else. When the time left in `budget_s` is below 1 s, the remaining invocations are not run, and their status is `"not_run"`. A missing or invalid `wrap.json` gives status `"invalid"`. - Values: for an invocation with status `ok`, a `trusted_wall` metric is `adapter_wall_s` plus its commands' `wall_s`, plus `eval_wall_s` when the design has an evaluator (null unless `eval_status` is `ok`). A `sealed_extraction` metric is its rule applied to the fetched file: the matched values are every `float()`-parsed match of the regex in order, or the number or array at the pointer. With `reduce` `first` or `max`, the value is that function of the matched values; with `value_at_max_key`, it is the value of the first pair whose key is the largest. A file under `eval` needs `eval_status` `ok`. A missing or unreadable file, no match, a nonfinite matched number, or a match count other than a non-null `expect_count` gives null. Every value of an invocation with any other status is null. A null value is a missing value. - Compute (G6): `A/results/evaluate/comparison_compute.json`, written atomically after the last invocation, is exactly `{invocations, arms, all_invocations, system, versions, allocation}`. - `invocations` has one row per scheduled invocation in run order, each exactly `{round, arm, input, status, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_status, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, attributed_usd}`, from `wrap.json`: `wall_s` is `adapter_wall_s` plus the commands' walls, and `attributed_usd` is `(wall_s + eval_wall_s) / 3600 * C/box.json.price_usd_h`, with a null wall counted as 0 and null when the price is unavailable. Rows of `not_run` invocations have null numbers. - `arms` has one row per arm, each exactly `{arm, invocations, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, eval_wall_s, eval_gpu_busy_s, attributed_usd}`, summed over that arm's replicate invocations whatever their status, with a null counted as 0; `gpu_busy_known` is true only when every summed row's flag is. - `all_invocations` is exactly `{invocations, wall_s, eval_wall_s, attributed_usd}`, summed over every row, warmups and failures included, with a null counted as 0. - `system` and `versions` copy the fetched `system.json` and `versions.json` (null when missing or invalid). - `allocation` is the bill of the whole box allocation, which may include work outside this run, exactly `{type, price_usd_h, started_utc, ended_utc, hours, usd, final}` from `C/box.json`. When that record has `ended_utc` and `hours`, they are copied and `final` is true; otherwise `ended_utc` is null, `hours` is the time from `started_utc` to when the file is written, and `final` is false. `usd` is `hours * price_usd_h`. Unavailable fields are null. At takeaways, after a matching allocation record refreshes `C/box.json` (see Compute metadata), the pipeline rewrites the file atomically with only `allocation` recomputed. The run's own share stays `run_box_usd`. Uploads, links, job files, user setup and fetches are outside every invocation row; they remain in the stage's receipts. - Scoring (U58): after the last invocation, `python3 -I m5/score_comparison.py `. Otherwise both contents are parsed as the output's `format` into number lists; different lengths, or a NaN in one list but not at the same position in the other, disagree; equal infinities agree; finite pairs agree when `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol` (`elementwise_abs`) or `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol + rel_tol * max(abs(a), abs(b))` (`elementwise_abs_plus_rel_max`). A pair agrees when every element agrees. Each compared pair records `max_abs_error` and `max_rel_error` over its finite elements (null when none). - Metric comparisons: an arm's value for (replicate, input) is the metric value above. For `pooled_mean`, a replicate's value is the mean over inputs, null when any input's value is null. With `"void"`, any missing value makes the unit void with reason `"missing_values"`. With `"fail"`, a missing value of `arm` makes the unit `"not_supported"` with reason `"missing_values"`, and otherwise a missing value of `against` makes it void with reason `"missing_values"`. - Eligibility (`given`): for each listed comparison, its outcome for this unit is that comparison's row for the same input when both comparisons are decided per input, and otherwise that comparison's outcome, where `"per_input"` counts as supported only when every row is. When any of these is not `"supported"`, the unit is void with reason `"not_eligible"`. - Interval: for `all_pairs`, `[lo, hi]` is the minimum and maximum of the differences, and needs at least one difference. For `bootstrap`, the ratio of means is recomputed on `bootstrap_resamples` resamples (`B`) with replacement of the unit's paired replicates, drawn from one `random.Random(bootstrap_seed)` stream in comparison order, and `[lo, hi]` is the `(1 - confidence) / 2` and `(1 + confidence) / 2` empirical quantiles (sorted resamples, index `floor(q * (B - 1))`); it needs at least two replicates. `estimate` is the mean difference (`all_pairs`) or the ratio of means (`bootstrap`) on the full data. Too few values gives outcome `"void"` with reason `"insufficient_replicates"`. - Margin value `m`: 0 for a null margin, `x` for `{"abs": x}`. - Outcome per decision unit, in this order: eligibility; then, for agreement, any compared pair that disagrees makes the unit not supported; then the missing-value rule; then the interval's minimum count; then the criterion. The criterion gives `"supported"`, `"not_supported"` or else `"inconclusive"`: agreement is supported when at least one pair was compared, every compared pair agrees and none is missing (with no compared pair, it is void with reason `"missing_values"`); non-inferiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo >= -m`, not supported when `hi < -m`; non-inferiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi <= m`, not supported when `lo > m`; superiority (`two_sided`) is supported when `lo > m` or `hi < -m`, not supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`; ratio with `strict` false is supported when `lo >= threshold`, not supported when `hi < threshold`; ratio with `strict` true is supported when `lo > threshold`, not supported when `hi <= threshold`. - `sign` of a unit is `"higher"` when a superiority is supported with `lo > m`, `"lower"` when it is supported with `hi < -m`, and null otherwise. - A comparison's outcome: for `pooled_mean`, its one unit's outcome; for `per_input_all`, supported when every input is supported, not supported when any input is not supported, void when any input is void and none is not supported, otherwise inconclusive; for `per_input_each`, `"per_input"`, with each input's outcome in its rows. - `C/comparison_scored.json`, atomic, is exactly `{comparison_sha256, comparisons, totals}`. `comparisons` follows the design's order, each exactly `{id, arm, against, criterion, unit, outcome, rows}`; `rows` has one row per decision unit (`input` null for `pooled_mean`), each exactly `{input, n, n_missing, estimate, lo, hi, margin_value, threshold, outcome, sign, reason, pairs}`. `n` counts the differences, ratios or compared pairs; `pairs` is null for metric comparisons and, for agreement, the per-replicate rows `{replicate, agrees, missing, max_abs_error, max_rel_error}` (`agrees` null and `missing` true when a side is missing). Numbers are null when void; `reason` is `"missing_values"`, `"insufficient_replicates"` or `"not_eligible"` for a void unit, `"missing_values"` for a unit made not supported by the `"fail"` rule, and null otherwise. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons. - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. A missing or invalid `wrap.json` or fetched file is not invalid input; it is a missing value. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`. - Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. Evaluate facts keep every existing key, null in comparison mode.

38	Your step folder is `experiments/blind-02/science/s16/`. Read `science/s09/`, `science/s13/`, `science/s14/` and `science/s15/` first (REQS.json, PARTS.json, FINAL.json, SHAPES.json, ASSESSMENT.md). s14 judged the operator's first draft `partial`; s15 gave each comparison's shape and the fixes (SHAPES.json). Judge also whether every fix and shape s15 chose is met, including any `other` you or s15 described; this is the operator's one revision, so a second `partial` goes to the owner with your assessment. It is a draft for a new section of `dut/pipeline/m5/SCHEMAS.md` (units U57 and U58), not yet committed, because the worktree is building U54 to U56. Judge whether it, as written, can express and decide each comparison K1..Kn of FINAL.json, run each arm, and record the compute facts FINAL.json asks for. 40	The contract section, verbatim:
41	
42	## Sealed comparison (U57, U58)
43	- Purpose: compare several published arms on one box under a design fixed before the run. Owner approval 2026-11-03 (contract gaps G1 comparison arms, G3 tolerance and equivalence, G6 compute metadata of the blind-02 science route); requirements from science steps s13 and s15. Arms are published programs or configurations that need no new code. Each invocation runs one arm on one input, and invocations are interleaved on one box. No agent computes a number: every number comes from the pipeline's trusted wall time, from rules fixed before the run and applied by the pipeline, or from a trusted comparator of two arms' outputs. Criteria, margins, reference values and thresholds are fixed by a science step before the run and hidden from the run's agents. Compute is recorded per invocation and covers the arm's own subprocess only. Never change a criterion after a result: every decision uses the sealed design. An outcome that is not supported is a result and never fails a stage. Comparisons that need more than one run are split by the science step into one design per run. Without `args.comparison`, every stage is unchanged.
44	- Optional `args.comparison` is an object with exactly the key `design`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a design JSON file. It is exclusive with `args.card`, `args.units_check` and `args.units_probe`. The design is exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, replicates, warmup, order_seed, budget_s, bootstrap_seed, comparisons}`:
45	  - `arms`: 2 to 5 items, each exactly `{id, what}`; ids `"A0"`, `"A1"`, ... in order; `what` a non-empty string. `A0` is the published baseline that intake and reproduce handle as usual.
46	  - `inputs`: 1 to 10 items, each exactly `{id, spec}`: `id` a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$`; `spec` any JSON value (pins, case, configuration).
47	  - `outputs`: 0 to 10 items, each exactly `{name, what, format}`: a logical result each arm writes for an input, compared across arms. `name` unique, matching `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,30}$`; `what` a non-empty string; `format` `"bytes"`, `"text_numbers"` (every number in the file's UTF-8 text, in order, as matched by `[-+]?(\d+\.?\d*|\.\d+)([eE][-+]?\d+)?` together with `nan`, `inf` and `-inf` tokens) or `"json_numbers"` (every number leaf of the JSON document, in document order; booleans are not numbers).

50	  - `comparisons`: 1 to 12 items, each exactly `{id, arm, against, measure, criterion, direction, unit, pairing, rule, confidence, margin, threshold, reference, parts}`:
51	    - `id` unique, matching `^K[0-9]{1,2}$`; `arm` an arm id; `against` a different arm id or `"reference"`; `parts` a non-empty array of unique non-empty strings.
52	    - `measure` is exactly `{metric}` (a metric name) or exactly `{output, comparator}` (an output name and one of `"exact"`, `"elementwise_abs"`, `"elementwise_rel"`, `"elementwise_abs_plus_rel"`). An output comparison needs an arm as `against`.
53	    - `criterion` `"equivalence"`, `"non_inferiority"`, `"superiority"`, `"ratio_at_least"` or `"agreement"`. `agreement` is the criterion of every output comparison and of no metric comparison.
54	    - `direction` `"higher_better"`, `"lower_better"` or `"two_sided"`: the metric as measured (for wall seconds, `lower_better`). `equivalence` and `agreement` use `two_sided`; `non_inferiority` and `ratio_at_least` use `higher_better` or `lower_better`; `superiority` takes any.
55	    - `unit` `"pooled_mean"` (each replicate's value is the mean over inputs, decided once), `"per_input_all"` (decided per input; the comparison holds only if it holds on every input) or `"per_input_each"` (decided and reported per input). `ratio_at_least` uses `pooled_mean`.
56	    - `pairing` `"paired_replicate"` or `"unpaired"`; output comparisons use `paired_replicate`.
57	    - `rule` `"all_pairs"` or `"bootstrap"`; `confidence` a number in `[0.5, 1)` for `bootstrap` and null for `all_pairs`. Output comparisons use `all_pairs`.
58	    - `margin`: null, `{"abs": x}`, `{"rel": y}` or `{"abs": x, "rel": y}` with `x` and `y` finite and nonnegative. For an output comparison it is the comparator's tolerance: `elementwise_abs` needs `abs`, `elementwise_rel` needs `rel`, `elementwise_abs_plus_rel` needs both, `exact` needs null. For a metric comparison it is null, `abs` or `rel`; `rel` scales by `abs(reference)` against a reference, else by `abs(mean of the against arm's values)` for the same unit.
59	    - `threshold`: a finite number above 0 for `ratio_at_least`, otherwise null.
60	    - `reference`: exactly when `against` is `"reference"`, an object `{source, values}`: `source` a non-empty string naming where the values come from (for example an earlier run of this route), `values` mapping every input id to a finite number; otherwise null.
61	  An invalid argument or design, or a path that cannot be read as JSON, fails intake with `error_class: parse` before any agent call.
62	- Before the intake agent call and any box command, the pipeline writes atomically, in this order: `C/comparison.json`, exactly `{source, source_sha256, design}`; `C/comparison_seal.json`, exactly `{comparison_sha256, sealed_utc}` (the SHA-256 of the exact bytes of `C/comparison.json`); and `A/comparison_view.json`, exactly `{arms, inputs, outputs, metrics, replicates, warmup}` copied from the design. The view holds no comparison, criterion, margin, threshold, reference value, part or budget. Agents see only the view; comparison-mode prompts name it and never `C/` or the design path. The science step that writes the design is responsible for the view's free text (`what`, `spec`) stating no expectation, criterion or result.
63	- Intake prompt, comparison mode only: the run compares the view's arms on the view's inputs; `A0` is the benchmark intake records as usual; intake also records, in `benchmark.json` under the key `arms`, each other arm's published source, pin and commands, and in `data.json` every input any arm needs.
64	- Harness prompt, comparison mode only: `setup.sh` also builds or installs every arm's published program and configuration, as published. The harness agent writes, besides the usual scripts:
65	  - one adapter `harness/arms/<arm id>.sh` per arm, `A0` included, that runs that arm's published program and configuration on the one input named by `CMP_INPUT` and writes its results under `CMP_OUT`; adapters never write or patch source, and never compute, write or assert a metric;
66	  - `harness/cmp_files.json`, exactly `{"files": {...}}`, mapping each arm id to an object that maps every output name to the relative path under `CMP_OUT` where that arm writes it;
67	  - `harness/cmp_extract.json`, exactly `{"rules": [...]}`, one rule per arm and `sealed_extraction` metric, each exactly `{arm, metric, file, kind, expr}`, with `file`, `kind` and `expr` as defined for `harness/card_extract.json` (U54) and `file` relative to `CMP_OUT`;
68	  - `harness/versions.sh`, which prints one JSON object mapping each arm id to its program's version string.
69	  Relative paths are one or more `/`-separated components made of `[A-Za-z0-9._+=-]`, none `.` or `..`. `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` keep their meaning for `A0`.
70	- After harness generation or copy (with `args.harness_from`, the source directory must also hold `arms/`, `cmp_files.json`, `cmp_extract.json` and `versions.sh`, copied like the scripts) and before the harness upload, those files must exist and be valid, and `harness/arms/` must hold exactly one non-empty adapter per arm; otherwise reproduce fails with `error_class: parse` before the upload. The pipeline then writes `C/arms_seal.json`, exactly `{files, sealed_utc}`, mapping each of those files' names (adapters as `arms/<id>.sh`) to the SHA-256 of its bytes. They upload with the harness, in the same encoding. No repair changes them.
71	- In comparison mode reproduce runs exactly as usual for `A0`. Profile, seal, propose and implement are SKIPPED. Evaluate runs the comparison when reproduce passed, and is SKIPPED otherwise, as after any failed gate.
72	- Evaluate, comparison mode (U57):
73	  - Versions: one box command, operation `versions`, runs `bash harness/versions.sh` with stdout to `out/comparison/versions.json`, then records CPU identity (`lscpu` model name and logical CPU count), the GPU driver and CUDA versions (`nvidia-smi`) and the kernel (`uname -r`) in `out/comparison/system.json`.
74	  - Rounds: `warmup` warmup rounds, then `replicates` replicate rounds. Each round runs every (arm, input) pair once, in an order drawn from one `random.Random(order_seed)` stream: one `shuffle` of the round's pairs per round, warmups included.
75	  - Each invocation is one box command, operation `comparison`, from the shared run directory. It builds a fresh `comparison-work/<round>/<arm>/<input>/` holding a symbolic link to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work`, `evaluation-work`, `units-check` and `comparison-work`, plus an empty `out/`, then runs the trusted wrapper `python3 profiler/cmp_wrap.py` (written inline by the pipeline, as the profile stage writes its probe). The wrapper runs `bash harness/arms/<arm>.sh` there and writes `out/cmp_wrap.json`, exactly `{rc, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known}`: the adapter's exit status (null on timeout), its `perf_counter` wall seconds, and GPU-busy seconds sampled while the adapter runs (`nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu` immediately and every second; each finite sample in [0,100] contributes `utilization / 100` seconds, summed over GPUs; `gpu_busy_known` false when no valid sample was taken). The environment carries `CMP_ARM`, `CMP_INPUT` (the input id), `CMP_INPUT_SPEC` (the JSON of that input's `spec`), `CMP_MODE` (`warmup` or `replicate`), `CMP_ROUND` (the index) and `CMP_OUT` (the absolute path of that `out/`). The invocation's `out/` is fetched to `A/results/evaluate/comparison/<w<k> or r<k>>/<arm>/<input>/`.
76	  - Each invocation's timeout is the time left in `budget_s` (and never past the run ceiling). When it is exhausted, the remaining invocations are not run and their values are null.
77	  - Values: for an invocation that ran with `rc` 0, a `trusted_wall` metric is its `wall_s`; a `sealed_extraction` metric is its rule applied to its fetched files (a missing or unreadable file, no match or a nonfinite value gives null). Every value of an invocation with a nonzero `rc`, a timeout or a missing wrapper file is null.
78	  - Compute (G6): `A/results/evaluate/comparison_compute.json`, written atomically after the last invocation, is exactly `{invocations, arms, system, versions, box}`. `invocations` has one row per invocation in run order, each exactly `{round, arm, input, rc, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, usd}`, from the wrapper, with `usd` = `wall_s / 3600 * C/box.json.price_usd_h` (null when the price is unavailable). `arms` has one row per arm, each exactly `{arm, invocations, wall_s, gpu_busy_s, gpu_busy_known, usd}`, summed over that arm's replicate invocations. `system` and `versions` copy the fetched files (null when missing or invalid), and `box` is exactly `{type, price_usd_h}` from `C/box.json`. Uploads, links and fetches are outside every row.
79	- Scoring (U58): after the last invocation, `python3 -I m5/score_comparison.py <C dir> <A/results/evaluate/comparison dir> <A/harness dir> <C/comparison_scored.json>`. It checks the SHA-256 of `C/comparison.json` against `C/comparison_seal.json` and of each sealed harness file against `C/arms_seal.json`, then scores each comparison from the replicate rounds only.
80	  - Output comparisons (`agreement`): for each input and replicate where both arms ran with `rc` 0, the comparator reads the mapped file of each arm. `exact`: identical bytes. Otherwise both files are parsed as the output's `format` into number lists; different lengths, or a NaN in one list but not at the same position in the other, disagree; equal infinities agree; finite pairs agree when `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol` (`elementwise_abs`), `abs(a - b) <= rel_tol * abs(b)` (`elementwise_rel`, `b` the `against` arm's element) or `abs(a - b) <= abs_tol + rel_tol * abs(b)` (`elementwise_abs_plus_rel`). A pair agrees when every element agrees. Each pair records `max_abs_error` and `max_rel_error` over its finite elements (null when none). A missing or unparsable file makes that pair missing.
81	  - Metric comparisons: an arm's value for (replicate, input) is the metric value above. For `pooled_mean`, a replicate's value is the mean over inputs, null when any input's value is null. The statistics are, per decision unit (the pooled value, or each input): for `paired_replicate`, the difference `arm - against` per replicate where both have values (or `arm - reference value`); for `unpaired`, the differences of every arm value with every against value (or with the reference value). `ratio_at_least` uses the ratio of means `mean(arm) / mean(against)` for `higher_better` and `mean(against) / mean(arm)` for `lower_better`, over the replicates where both have values.
82	  - Interval: for `all_pairs`, `[lo, hi]` is the minimum and maximum of the differences (for a ratio, of the per-replicate ratios in the same orientation), and needs at least one difference. For `bootstrap`, the statistic (the mean difference, or the ratio of means) is recomputed on 10000 resamples with replacement of the unit's paired replicates (for `unpaired`, of each arm's values separately), drawn from one `random.Random(bootstrap_seed)` stream in comparison order, and `[lo, hi]` is the `(1 - confidence) / 2` and `(1 + confidence) / 2` empirical quantiles (sorted resamples, index `floor(q * 9999)`); it needs at least two replicates. `estimate` is the statistic on the full data. Too few values gives outcome `"void"` with reason `"insufficient_replicates"`; no values at all gives reason `"missing_values"`.
83	  - Margin value `m`: 0 for a null margin, `x` for `{"abs": x}`, and for `{"rel": y}` `y * abs(reference value)` or `y * abs(mean of the against arm's values in the unit)`.
84	  - Outcome per decision unit, `"supported"`, `"not_supported"` or else `"inconclusive"`: agreement is supported when every pair agrees and none is missing, not supported when any pair disagrees, otherwise void with reason `"missing_values"`; equivalence is supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`, not supported when `hi < -m` or `lo > m`; non-inferiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo >= -m`, not supported when `hi < -m`; non-inferiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi <= m`, not supported when `lo > m`; superiority (`higher_better`) is supported when `lo > m`, not supported when `hi <= m`; superiority (`lower_better`) is supported when `hi < -m`, not supported when `lo >= -m`; superiority (`two_sided`) is supported when `lo > m` or `hi < -m`, not supported when `-m <= lo` and `hi <= m`; ratio is supported when `lo >= threshold`, not supported when `hi < threshold`.
85	  - A comparison's outcome: for `pooled_mean`, its one unit's outcome; for `per_input_all`, supported when every input is supported, not supported when any input is not supported, void when any input is void and none is not supported, otherwise inconclusive; for `per_input_each`, `"per_input"`, with each input's outcome in its rows.
86	  - `C/comparison_scored.json`, atomic, is exactly `{comparison_sha256, comparisons, totals}`. `comparisons` follows the design's order, each exactly `{id, arm, against, criterion, unit, outcome, rows}`; `rows` has one row per decision unit (`input` null for `pooled_mean`), each exactly `{input, n, estimate, lo, hi, margin_value, threshold, outcome, reason, pairs}`. `n` counts the differences, ratios or compared pairs; `pairs` is null for metric comparisons and, for agreement, the per-replicate rows `{replicate, agrees, max_abs_error, max_rel_error}`. Numbers are null when void; `reason` is null unless void. `totals` is exactly `{supported, not_supported, inconclusive, void}`, counting decision units over all comparisons.
87	  - Exit 0 after writing; exit 1 for invalid or missing input, a seal mismatch or a failed write, with no output file. Diagnostics contain no input content. A scoring failure fails evaluate with `error_class: parse`.
88	- Evaluate status in comparison mode is PASS once `C/comparison_scored.json` was written, whatever the outcomes. Evaluate facts keep every existing key, null in comparison mode, and add optional `comparisons_total`, `comparisons_supported`, `comparisons_not_supported`, `comparisons_inconclusive` and `comparisons_void` (decision units, nonnegative integers), all null outside comparison mode, on SKIPPED/stub records and whenever the scored file was not written; records without them stay valid.
89	
90	Write `CHECK.json`: exactly `{"gaps": "G1+G3+G6", "verdict": ..., "missing": [...], "problems": [...]}`:
91	- `"verdict"`: `"sufficient"` (build as written), `"partial"` (build after the listed fixes), `"insufficient"` (this design cannot serve these gaps).
92	- `"missing"`: the ids of FINAL.json's arms (`"A0"`...) and comparisons (`"K1"`...) this contract cannot run, express or decide as FINAL.json needs, plus `"compute_facts"` when a listed compute fact is not recorded; no duplicates; empty if none.
93	- `"problems"`: codes, no duplicates, empty if none, from: `"arm_not_runnable"` (an arm cannot be run by an adapter of published code and configuration), `"metric_not_capturable"` (a metric cannot come from the adapter or the trusted wall time), `"criterion_unfit"` (a criterion's decision rule is not what the question needs), `"statistic_unfit"` (the replicate aggregation, pairing, interval rule or small-sample rule cannot decide it), `"margin_rule_unfit"` (absolute or relative margins, or their base, are wrong for a comparison), `"reference_unfit"` (a fixed reference value cannot serve), `"order_unfit"` (the interleaving, warmups or seeds are wrong), `"inputs_unfit"` (inputs per invocation, or averaging over them, are wrong), `"budget_unfit"` (the evaluate budget cannot hold the rounds), `"compute_unfit"` (the compute record is wrong or incomplete), `"leaks_or_biases"` (an agent could see criteria, margins, references or ratios, or steer an arm), `"sealing_unfit"`, `"other"`.
94	
95	Write `ASSESSMENT.md` for the owner: your judgement in prose, and for each missing item or problem the smallest fix. Write `NARROWING.md` ("No narrowing." with the reason, or what changed), `PREDICTIONS.md` ("No test; no predictions."), `predictions.json` `{"items": []}`, `outcomes.json` `{"items": []}` (s15 sealed none), and `NEXT.json` `{"action": "stop", "reason": "contract_gap"}`. CHECK.json holds no free text and no seed content.
96	
97	`status.json`: one JSON object with exactly these keys, each taking only the listed values:
98	- `"verdict"`: `"sufficient"`, `"partial"`, `"insufficient"` (as in CHECK.json)
99	- `"missing_count"`: `"none"`, `"one"`, `"two_or_more"`
100	- `"problem_count"`: `"none"`, `"one"`, `"two_or_more"`
101	- `"next_action"`: `"stop"`
102	- `"stop_reason"`: `"contract_gap"`
103	- `"narrowing"`: `"none"`, `"explicit"`
104	- `"prediction_count"`: `"none"`
105	
106	No other keys and no free text. Finish within 30 minutes.

You are the scientific agent for the blind-02 experiment of the metis repository (`/home/hal/dev/interp/metis`). The owner authorized you to read its seed and records. The operator who launches you is blind: it sees only your `status.json`, validated as fixed enum values, plus file counts and hashes. Your other files are for the owner and for the next scientific step, never for the operator. Never put seed or record content into `status.json`.

## The owner's request (2026-11-03), which binds every step
The owner's impression is that run2 exposed a limitation of m5's fixed menu, while the seed's original question remains open; check that against the run's evidence. The repo has a tree/card mechanism for exploring experiments under a fixed root question, and a measure route for calibrating the cards' assumptions. Use them to continue within this seed: find candidate experiments that address different parts of the question, and inexpensive measurements that distinguish between them; carry promising candidates through calibration. You prepare the scientific inputs, including `tree_args.json`. After each result you assess what it supports and choose the next informative test. Seal predictions before each test, preserve negative results, and make any narrowing of the question explicit. If an existing mechanism cannot express a required comparison, identify the specific contract gap (file, section, what it cannot express). Stop when there is no justified next test, the limits are reached, or the owner's input is genuinely necessary.

## Where things are (paths relative to the repo root)
- Seed and materials: `experiments/blind-02/m5/BRIEF.md` (the owner's seed, verbatim) and `experiments/blind-02/m5/b01_materials/BRIEF_run1.md` (seed plus a materials addendum copied from blind-01 records).
- m5 runs: `experiments/blind-02/m5/run1/` (intake PASS, reproduce infra failure) and `run2/` (stopped at propose, outcome no_feasible_method). Earlier readers: `m5/run2_progress2/REPORT.md`, `m5/run2_trace/REPORT.md` (a full trace of the seed's comparisons through run2; build on it rather than redo it).
- blind-01 records on the same materials, read-only, if they bear on a candidate: `experiments/blind-01/m5/` (run9 reproduce at reduced scale; run10 unit equivalence; run11 unit concurrency probe).
- Earlier science steps: `experiments/blind-02/science/sNN/` (read all earlier steps before writing).
- Tree/card: `dut/pipeline/launch.js` (kinds `tree`, `card`, `measure`), `dut/pipeline/CONTRACT.md` (question_tree_v2: section 2.5 PLAN, section 5 "Seed records" and "calibration"), `dut/pipeline/src/main.js` (args at lines 15-35; calibration records near line 468), `src/prompts.js`, `src/schemas.js`. `launch.js <exp> tree --seed <args.json>` lays your file over `experiments/question-tree/replay/args_F.json` (minus its `fixed_roots` and `base`). Keys: `seed` (integer), `fixed_roots` (root questions held fixed), `seed_ideas` (strings or option records `{title, text, root_question, kind, root_link, compute_open, sequential, source_urls}`; each becomes its own pick and card), `picks_per_branch`, `pool_k`, `require_compute_lever`, `deepen_on_signal`, `budget_usd`, `budget_covers_storage`, `budget_covers_tax`. The tree writes `experiments/blind-02/<stamp>-tree/out/result.json` with `cards`, `table`, `inventory`, `calibration[]` (state `not_judged|rejected|calibration_required|no_unmeasured_input`, `plan_usd`, `required[]` load-bearing GUESS/PROXY inputs with their measuring phase).
- Measure: `launch.js <exp> measure --card <tree run> --pick <key>` compiles one calibration record into a latent_skeptic measure folder (QUESTION.md, SEALED_PREDICTIONS.md, out/triage_args.json, CARD.json) with no model call; it checks each GUESS/PROXY input against a ratio band (2.5x PROXY, 3x otherwise) and does not carry the card's arms or decision rule (`launch.js:58-107`). The stages after it (design, gate, build, tests, review, launch, post) run via `launch.js <exp> stage --measure <dir> --stage ...` on `idea/wf.js`, but the script that wrote their args files and chained them (m4's `measure.sh`) is not available to this route; treat the measure route's execution as unproven, and say what a calibration would need from it.
- m5: `dut/pipeline/m5/SCHEMAS.md`, `pipeline.js`. It can also run a calibration on a box: `~/.cache/blind01/new_run.py` options `--stop-after-reproduce` (setup and anchors only), `--stop-after-profile` (adds the profile and the concurrency probe), `--units-check=run<N>`, `--units-probe=run<N>`, `--harness-from=<dir>`.

## Limits (the operator enforces them; plan within them)
